 Around Town: November 2026
 By GIH Staff 
 Published: November 2, 2026 | Updated: November 1, 2026 | Calendar Tags: arts and culture | community events | community resources | family activities | free events | germantown | holiday markets | local workshops | Northwest Philly | November events | outdoor activities | Thanksgiving 
 Events and happenings around Germantown this month.
 Germantown Night Market in July 2025. (Photo: Rasheed Z. Ajamu)
 November brings a full slate of events to Germantown.
 This month’s events, whether Thanksgiving-themed, nature-based, or resource workshops, will invite neighbors to get outside and connect.
 The Germantown Info Hub compiled this list of free, low-cost, and ticketed events for neighbors to explore.
 Throughout November : Local poet Raina Leon is OH2’s November 2026 Artist in Residence, and she brings Swing Mezzo: Archive Alive to life throughout the month. The event series lets community members experience Black jazz history through poetry, original music, visual art, archival projections, and community storytelling. Most events take place at OH2 at 6376 Germantown Ave.
 Nov. 2: The Alexander Advantage LLC is hosting a college FAFSA completion workshop at the Joseph E. Coleman Library, 68 W. Chelten Ave., from 4:30–6:30 p.m. Parents and students can learn about FAFSA and financial aid, start an application, and connect with a college prep professional.
 Nov. 3: Neighborhood Community Action Center 8 will host SuccessPhilly from 1–3 p.m. at Joseph E. Coleman Northwest Regional Library, 68 W. Chelten Ave. Visitors can meet one-on-one with a professional from the city’s Office of Human Resources to learn about job opportunities and hiring processes.
 Nov. 3: The Wedeniche Art Studio is hosting its Falling Into Place: Paint and Sip Workshop at Salam Cafe, 5532 Greene Street, from 5:30-8 p.m. It’s an autumn-themed paint-and-sip activity for neighbors; tickets are $23.18. Visit here to register.
 Nov. 4: The School District of Philadelphia and Diversity with Aquatics are holding a Community Film Screening from 4:30-7:30 p.m. at the James Logan School (1700 Lindley Ave.). The film, When Everyone Swims, will be shown that evening and explores water safety, access to swimming education, and the barriers that have impacted disparities in drowning rates. The movie will start at 5. Visit here to register.
 Nov. 5: Friends of the Wissahickon (FOW) will host a Trail Planning Open House from 4:30-7:30 p.m. at the Weavers Way Germantown Outreach Office (326 W Chelten Ave. # B). There, neighbors can help shape the future of FOW’s All Persons Trail, which will be constructed in Wissahickon Valley Park. Folks are welcome to offer accessible alternatives to the park’s existing trails. Visit here to learn more.
 Nov. 7: The Awbury Arboretum, 1 Awbury Road, is hosting Fall Tree Planting from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., where neighbors can join in. Awbury plans to add up to 100 new trees to its collection, and tree tenders from across the Northwest will guide the planting and assist participants. Folks can see a tree-planting overview and demo. Register here . 
 Nov. 7 : Edssentials is hosting its Cleanovation Lab from 10:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at Awbury Arboretum (1 Awbury Road). There, youth ages 3-9 can embark on a hands-on science adventure, including a scavenger hunt through the arboretum to identify what belongs in nature. Visit here to register and learn more.
 Nov. 7: The Maplewood Collective will hold its Germantown Night Market at Maplewood Mall from 4-9 p.m., featuring a variety of food, artisan, clothing, accessory, and art vendors, plus more.
 Nov. 7 : Join Philly Deaf & CODA Fam for “Fam, Food & Good Vibes” from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. at Joseph E. Coleman Northwest Regional Library (68 W Chelten Ave.). Bring food to share and sit together. American Sign Language (ASL) will be the primary language used during the event. Questions or concerns: [email protected] .
 Nov. 8 : Join the Open Mic Night at the W. Duval Community Garden. It’s a great opportunity to connect with your neighbors. The entrance is located between 235 and 237 W. Duval. For more information or to perform, please contact Carlos at (215) 581-1858 or email [email protected] .
 Nov. 8 : Can your vote be your voice, and yet not the only way to have one? Join Unmasking the Vote , from 2–4 p.m., at G-Town Radio (24 Maplewood Mall), the final Chat & Chew gathering of the #10YearsofRacismIsASickness residency. Ideas about voting, opposing perspectives, and the experiences that complicate what people believe. RSVP by Nov. 1 .
 Nov. 9: The Mt. Airy CDC is hosting its Northwest Philly Small Business Summit from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. at NewCourtland’s conference facilities (6950 Germantown Ave). The summit will feature practical workshops, expert panel discussions, networking opportunities, and breakfast to empower local Northwest Philly businesses. Tickets are $30. Visit here to learn more about registration and what’s included.
 Nov. 11: The Pennsylvania Barber School, 5843 Germantown Ave., will be offering free haircuts for Veterans from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. 
 Nov. 14: Historic Germantown is holding its Belfield Winghocking Walking Tour from 1-3 p.m., starting and ending at the La Salle University Art Museum at 1900 W. Olney Ave. The walk is about 2 miles and takes you through La Salle’s campus and around parts of the campus perimeter along Lindley and Belfield Avenues. It will cover certain late-18th-century historical buildings. Visit here to register.
 Nov. 14: Cliveden of the National Trust, 6401 Germantown Ave., is holding a closing reception for its Looking Glass art installation from 3-5 p.m. Since May, the exhibition has reflected on the history of people and places in commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary. The house will be open for self-guided walkthroughs of the installation. Visit here to learn more.
 Nov. 20–21 : Shop more than 70 local makers at Waldorf’s Holiday Fair & Craft Bazaar, 6000 Wayne Ave. Adults-only shopping runs Friday, Nov. 20, 6–10 p.m.; family fun follows Saturday, Nov. 21, 10 a.m.–4 p.m. Admission is free; children’s activities require tickets. Get the details here . 
 Nov 20: The PA Flax Project will host its flax processing demonstration at the Wyck Historic House, 6026 Germantown Ave., from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Visitors will see how the flax crop becomes a spinnable fiber used to make many different items. Visit here to register.
 Nov. 21: The Germantown Community Fridge will host its Neighbor’s Table event at the First United Methodist Church of Germantown, 6001 Germantown Ave., from 12–2 p.m. The community will enjoy free meals with vegetarian and meat options.
 Nov. 24: Center in the Park (CIP), 5818 Germantown Ave., will hold its Thanksgiving Luncheon at 11 a.m., where neighbors can enjoy a Thanksgiving meal and live entertainment. Tickets are $7 for members and $10 for non-members and can be purchased at CIP’s program office on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.
 Have an event for this month or next to add to the list? Send it to [email protected] or text (215) 383-2664 .
